title: Allow-list the filesystem paths the mesh routes accept
body:
## Summary
mesh-finish, view-gate and ue-import take arbitrary absolute paths, and mesh-finish creates the output directory before anything else uses it.

## Description
src/app/api/visual-gen/mesh-finish/route.ts takes highPolyPath and outputPath and calls mkdirSync on dirname(outputPath). src/app/api/visual-gen/view-gate/route.ts takes meshPath, referencePath and outDir. src/app/api/visual-gen/ue-import/route.ts takes glbPath. Remediate and mesh-split already resolve a basename inside the ASSET_DIRS allow-list, and their headers name that contrast. Fixed means the same allow-list on all three, or a recorded decision that absolute paths stay.

## Flow
- operator POSTs outputPath anywhere -> mkdirSync creates the tree -> Blender writes there
- proposal: resolve input and output against generated/ allow-listed dirs, then migrate external callers

## Expected impact
Closes arbitrary directory creation and file write. Could break a caller that passes a path outside generated/, such as a UE project file.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - inputs and outputs confined to allow-listed dirs
Before: 0 of 3 routes confine paths; 2 sibling routes do
After: 3 of 3 confine, or a recorded exception
Method: probe - read of the five routes; caller census outside generated/ not run
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: contract

title: Admit Blender and editor jobs through a concurrency limit
body:
## Summary
The three mesh job stores start every job immediately and never evict a finished one.

## Description
src/lib/visual-gen/mesh-finish-job-store.ts, view-gate-job-store.ts and ue-import-job-store.ts have 0 concurrency limits and 0 Map deletes. N POSTs mean N concurrent Blender or editor processes, on a machine that has already been crashed by one 211 GB mesh run. The job store files belong to visual-gen-mesh-quality-gates and contact-sheet-ue5-export, so this is outside this context.

## Flow
- script POSTs ten mesh-finish jobs -> ten Blender processes start at once
- proposal: one admission queue per process class, with a capped retained-job count

## Expected impact
A burst queues instead of exhausting memory. A queued job reads as running for longer unless status reports it.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - bounded concurrent spawns
Before: 0 limits, 0 evictions across 3 stores (grep)
After: unmeasured
Method: probe - grep of the three stores; no load run
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: A vitest with injected fake runners: POST 10 jobs, assert the peak concurrent runner count equals the limit and retained jobs stay capped.

title: pof-mcp sends no operator token to the routes it calls
body:
## Summary
The MCP client posts with Content-Type only, so a deployment that sets POF_OPERATOR_TOKEN answers 401 to pof_asset_view_gate.

## Description
tools/pof-mcp/src/pofClient.ts:40 sets only Content-Type, and a grep for the token header in tools/pof-mcp/src returned 0 hits. requireOperator allows header-less calls only when no token is configured. This round added the guard to view-gate; the same gap already applied to every guarded route the MCP calls.

## Flow
- set POF_OPERATOR_TOKEN -> pof_asset_view_gate POSTs without it -> 401
- proposal: pofClient reads the token from env and sends x-operator-token

## Expected impact
MCP-driven gates keep working on a token-protected server. Nothing changes where no token is set.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - MCP works with the token set
Before: 0 token headers in tools/pof-mcp/src
After: 1 client-level header
Method: probe - grep; not run against a token-set server
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: A pofClient unit test with POF_OPERATOR_TOKEN set asserting the header is sent, plus one live MCP call against a token-set dev server.

title: Cap the scene-decompose image and hint size
body:
## Summary
scene-decompose decodes an imageDataUrl of any size and forwards a hint of any length into the vision prompt.

## Description
src/app/api/visual-gen/scene-decompose/route.ts decodes the whole data URL into a Buffer and crops it once per prop. No byte ceiling exists on the image or on hint.

## Flow
- caller posts a very large data URL -> full decode in process -> vision call billed on it
- proposal: refuse above a measured ceiling with a 413

## Expected impact
Oversized uploads are refused before decode and billing. A ceiling set too low would refuse real scene art.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - bounded decode
Before: no ceiling on image or hint (read)
After: unmeasured
Method: probe - read; real scene size distribution not sampled
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: Sample the byte sizes of real scene art in generated/ and scene-composer use to pick the ceiling, then a route test at ceiling+1.

title: Refuse an unknown assetClass on ue-import and remediate
body:
## Summary
mesh-finish now refuses an unknown assetClass; ue-import, its plan and remediate still grade class-blind.

## Description
src/app/api/visual-gen/mesh-finish/route.ts checks ASSET_CLASS_IDS after this round. src/app/api/visual-gen/ue-import/route.ts, src/app/api/visual-gen/ue-import/plan/route.ts and src/app/api/visual-gen/mesh-finish/remediate/route.ts accept any string and report class-blind grading in gradedAs. That report is honest, so this is a contract choice: a typo costs the budget check and the scale nominal, but free-form classes may be in use.

## Flow
- POST assetClass=charcter -> graded class-blind -> no scale nominal
- proposal: census sent classes, then refuse the unknown

## Expected impact
Typos surface at the door. Would break a caller relying on free-form classes.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one assetClass rule across routes
Before: 1 of 4 routes refuses
After: 4 of 4
Method: probe - read; caller census not run
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: contract
instrument: A census of assetClass values reaching the three routes from the panels and MCP tools; refuse only if every value is in ASSET_CLASS_IDS.

title: Require assetName on POST ue-import as the preview does
body:
## Summary
The plan route refuses a missing assetName; the import route accepts it and lands on the shared default.

## Description
src/app/api/visual-gen/ue-import/plan/route.ts requires assetName because an unnamed import lands on /Game/Generated/TripoSRMesh and replaces the last one, and its header says the refusals mirror the import route. src/app/api/visual-gen/ue-import/route.ts still treats it as optional. The panel always sends a name; direct callers may not.

## Flow
- direct POST without assetName -> shared TripoSRMesh replaced
- proposal: require it, as the plan does

## Expected impact
Closes the silent overwrite. A breaking contract change for any direct caller.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - preview and import agree
Before: plan refuses, import accepts
After: both refuse
Method: probe - read of both routes
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: contract

title: Decide whether scene-decompose gates crops by default
body:
## Summary
A direct call pays one vision call per prop unless it opts out; the UI always opts out by default.

## Description
src/app/api/visual-gen/scene-decompose/route.ts runs the crop gate unless gateCrops is false, while useSceneDressStore defaults it to false and sends it explicitly. The two defaults disagree, and props can be numerous. This round corrected the comment that called it opt-in; the behaviour is a product choice.

## Flow
- direct POST without gateCrops -> one vision call per prop

## Expected impact
Direct callers get a predictable bill, or the panel gets the gate by default.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - one default for a billed step
Before: 2 disagreeing defaults
After: 1 default
Method: probe - read
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
